To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the private libraries of the colonial period in Peru, in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, were small and contained few titles.

the number of books circulating in the colonial society of Peru was very small, that they were mostly in Spanish and that they were imported mainly from Spain, but also from other parts of the Hispanic world.
the private library of a colonial Peruvian was not an exception in the early modern world, but rather a common practice among the educated elite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of books as vehicles of ideas, and the ways in which they contributed to the development of a colonial society.
the diffusion of books and ideas in the viceroyalties of Peru.
the study of the circulation of books and ideas in the colonial world of Peru.

the book is a cultural artifact, a social product, a historical phenomenon that reflects the values, the ideas, and the social and economic structure of the society in which it is printed and distributed.3 The study of private libraries is an important approach to the history of ideas, for it reveals the intellectual interests and the reading habits of the members of a particular society.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of the history of books in colonial Peru, although it has been a long-standing concern of Peruvian scholars and historians, is still in a preliminary stage.
the history of books is a key element to understand the cultural history of the viceroyalties.
